priorities.finding: Prioritize request_context (tab, hour, weekday) as the only screened group with positive aggregate primary lift (+0.00221) and full coverage. Its within-user ranking evidence is directionally useful across cold-user and warm-user/item slices, although daily variability is material and the lift is not uniformly positive.
priorities.recommended_action: Retain request_context in the next budgeted model iteration, but require temporal stability checks and confirm gains on a fresh holdout before production rollout.

priorities.finding: Reject the remaining screened feature groups. Each has a negative aggregate primary lift, including strongly negative results for historical author/item response and item metadata; the occasional positive daily slices do not overcome the negative overall evidence.
priorities.recommended_action: Do not spend additional experiment budget on these groups in their current form. Revisit only with a separately justified redesign, strict temporal availability controls, and new train-only screening.

avoid: Do not use current-impression outcome fields for ranking; they are unavailable at decision time and would constitute leakage.
Do not promote aggregate snapshot statistics without per-impression availability timestamps; historical response and item-level statistics require temporal reconstruction before reconsideration.

Do not treat user_positive_count segments as deployable feature evidence: the diagnostic explicitly uses validation labels retrospectively, and the zero-positive slice has GAUC 0.5 with zero top-five retrieval quality.

Do not infer broad robustness from high GAUC alone. The weakest tab slice has GAUC 0.3519 and nDCG@5 0.0263, while hour 3 has GAUC 0.5121 and nDCG@5 0.3860, showing that top-five ranking weaknesses can remain severe even when discrimination is near chance.
metric_diagnosis: Experiment 2 reaches global GAUC 0.6694, nDCG@5 0.5367, and primary 0.6030, but it provides no observed primary improvement over the parent despite the predicted gain. Under the strict early-stopping budget rule, stop further experimentation now. Post-score diagnostics are validation slices rather than independent test estimates: tab 8 is the clearest operational weakness, with GAUC 0.3519, nDCG@5 0.0263, and primary 0.1891, while the large warm-item-frequency segment is essentially global (GAUC 0.6686, nDCG@5 0.5366, primary 0.6026). Focus any future work on low-performing tabs and top-five ranking quality, not on GAUC-only optimization.
